notes: Cat-form DPS at 60: Rake kept ticking, Shred building combo points, Rip as the 5-point finisher (Ferocious Bite once Rip is already up), Tiger's Fury taken on cooldown for the free energy. The fork's feral_druid/apls/feral.apl.json is the sim-tuned version of this same idea, but it names spell ids (17392, 9846, 13494, 17061, ...) that do not exist in this build's spellconst -- stale from an older client, exactly the kind of drift design section notes warn about -- so p1.apl.json (its minimal Shred-only fallback) is the starting point actually adapted here, filled out to a full finisher rotation with ranks checked against spellconst: Shred rank 5 (9830), Rake rank 4 (9904), Rip rank 6 (9896), Ferocious Bite rank 5 (31018), Tiger's Fury (5217, rankless). This spec stays in Cat Form for its entire rotation. Fix round 3: sim/druid/tigers_fury.go registers one id per level bracket and gives a level-60 druid 9846, not 5217 (the level-25 rank this file names); 9846 is not in this build's spellconst -- the same 'stale from an older client' gap the paragraph above already documents for the fork's own feral.apl.json preset, which names 9846 among the ids it drops for exactly that reason -- so there is no engine-castable id to switch to yet, and 5217 is declared inert instead of renamed. The line is kept: it is the guide's own placement and upgrades itself once spellconst carries 9846. Bear Form is not modeled here: Maul (48480) is the on-next-swing tank ability the engine keys off ON_NEXT_SWING_QUEUE_TAG, but the fork's own sim/druid/_maul.go is underscore-prefixed (excluded from its build) because bear-form tank druid is not implemented yet, so no rotation -- this one included -- can name 48480 today. Powershifting (Furor + Wolfshead Helm energy refunds on shifting out of and back into Cat Form), which the community guide treats as core to Classic Feral DPS, is a talent- and gear-dependent technique the APL value language here does not have a clean way to express yet; left out of the default, matching the measured-simplicity precedent set by mage-frost. Fix round 1: re-verified both dotIsActive conditions against the engine, since an id merely existing in spellconst is not enough (a totem-style buff/dummy split elsewhere in this fork resolves to a nil condition -- see shaman-enhancement's notes). sim/druid/rake.go and sim/druid/rip.go both set ActionID: core.ActionID{SpellID: <rank id>} directly on the spell, and their Dot lives on that same spell object (dotIsActive resolves via GetAPLSpell -> spell.Dot(target), not via a separate aura registry), so dotIsActive(9904) and dotIsActive(9896) both correctly find their DoTs. No change needed.

expected_idle.reason: Ferocious Bite only fires at 5 combo points while Rip still has more than 6s left (the branch above it refreshes Rip instead). The engine's Rip carries a fixed 12s duration rather than one that scales with combo points (engine lane 1's report), and this bare ladder build's only combo generator is Shred, which reaches 5 combo points slower than a talented/geared build would -- by the time 5 combo points are banked, Rip (refreshed under 6s remaining) has already used up most of its 12s window again, so the Bite branch is structurally unreachable on this build. The line is kept for a geared/talented character where it is reachable; not a rotation defect.

sources.label: Warcraft Tavern: WoW Classic Feral Druid DPS rotation

priorityList.notes: Tiger's Fury on cooldown for the free energy; it costs nothing and the engine gates it on its own 30 second cooldown.
Keep Rake ticking; it is a strong bleed that costs no combo point.

At 5 combo points, Rip once it has under 6s left. Fix round: the engine's Rip carries a fixed 12s duration rather than one that scales with combo points (engine lane 1's report), and this bare build's only combo generator is Shred, which reaches 5 combo points slower than a talented/geared build would -- gating the refresh on `not dotIsActive` meant Rip was ALWAYS already expired by the time 5 combo points arrived, so the branch below (Ferocious Bite with Rip up) was unreachable every time, not just occasionally. dotRemainingTime < 6s refreshes a little before the DoT actually falls off, the same clip-avoidance shape as warrior-arms' Rend upkeep, and leaves the Bite branch below reachable whenever Rip still has real time on it.

At 5 combo points with Rip having more than 6s left, Ferocious Bite dumps them instead of capping out. Fix round: paired with the dotRemainingTime rewrite above, this is the branch engine lane 1's report found unreachable under the engine's fixed 12s Rip.
Shred builds combo points the rest of the time.

Claw is a fallback builder below level 22, before Shred is learned (druid.md audit finding 2). Shred (learn level 22) is dropped by rewriteRotationRanks below that level, leaving nothing castable at 20-21 without this line. The audit's own recommendation named spellranks.json's rank-1 id (1082, learn level 20); investigating that with the scratch test at level 20 found it does NOT actually cast under this engine build. sim/druid/claw.go's registerClawSpell() registers ONE spell with a hardcoded ActionID{SpellID: 9850} -- spellranks.json's own rank-5/level-58 Claw id -- called unconditionally with no per-rank loop at all, unlike sim/druid/shred.go (shredSpellID[rank]) and sim/druid/rake.go (rakeRank.id) in the same package, which both register one spell per rank the way the rank-rewrite system expects. request.go's rotation() only calls rewriteRotationRanks below api.MaxLevel ('the rotation was authored for exactly the ranks it already carries' at 60, so the rewrite is skipped there) -- every OTHER entry in this file is written at its level-60 rank (Shred rank5/9830, Rake rank4/9904, ...) for exactly that reason, so this line is written the same way, at 9850/rank5, the id the engine actually registers, rather than at the audit's rank-1 id. That makes it fire correctly at level 60 (see cast tables) and, below level 58, rewriteRotationRanks's family-based lookup (any id belonging to a ranked spell resolves to the CURRENTLY LEARNED rank, regardless of which specific rank id the source names) still rewrites it down to 1082-9849, none of which the engine ever registers -- so the line remains genuinely inert for the level 20-21 window it exists for, an engine gap (Claw needs the same per-rank registration Shred and Rake already have), not something fixable from the rotation lane. Left in at 9850/rank5 since it is both the textually correct current-max reference and the id that already works at 60; it becomes real below level 58 too the moment claw.go is fixed to register one spell per rank the way Shred and Rake do. Flagged for the engine lane.
